input.question: If our atmosphere was 78% Oxygen instead of nitrogen, would we be able to hold our breath longer?
input.ground_truth: If we hadn't been killed off by fires raging across continents every time there was a lightning storm, or exterminated by gigantic insects, sure. P.S. Insects are limited in size by their relatively inefficient pulmonary systems (and, possibly, their exoskeletons).

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: If our atmosphere was 78% Oxygen instead of nitrogen, would we be able to hold our breath longer?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay, let’s imagine the air around us is like a big jar of jelly beans. Right now, most of the jelly beans are one color (that’s nitrogen), and only a few are red (that’s oxygen).

Now, if the jar had lots and lots more red jelly beans (that’s if the air was mostly oxygen), it would be different for our bodies. You see, when you hold your breath, your body needs a special kind of jelly bean (oxygen) to help your body work. But too many red jelly beans in the air can actually be bad for you, even when you are breathing.

If the air was 78% oxygen, it would be too much oxygen for our lungs and body. It could hurt us, even if we try to hold our breath. So, we might not be able to hold our breath longer; instead, it might make us feel funny or even get sick.

So, having too much oxygen in the air is not good for us, even if we want to hold our breath!
